$comment: Schema for a single skill JSON file. Fields marked (embedded) are concatenated into the text that gets embedded for cosine-similarity matching. Fields marked (display) are shown in the UI. Fields marked (agent) are passed to the LLM reranker on top-k candidates.
id: string — kebab-case unique identifier, must match the filename without .json. (display, agent)
name: string — short human title, 2 to 6 words. Shown as the card headline. (embedded, display, agent)
problem: string — one sentence describing the pain this skill solves, phrased from the user's perspective. 10 to 25 words. (embedded, display, agent)
when_to_use: string — one sentence describing the trigger situation. Start with 'Use when...'. 10 to 25 words. (embedded, display, agent)
tags: string — 3 to 6 lowercase single-word tags. Used for filtering AND embedded as keywords. Examples: writing, summarization, code, planning, feedback.
use_cases: string — 3 to 6 short phrases (5 to 12 words each) a user might literally type when looking for this skill. These do the heaviest lifting for retrieval, so write them in natural query language, not formal descriptions.
instructions: string — the prompt / system message / workflow the skill executes. Can be multi-paragraph. NOT embedded (kept out of the vector to avoid retrieval noise from generic phrasing). Shown on the detail page. (display, agent)

example.input: string — a realistic sample input a user might paste in. (display, agent)
example.output: string — what the skill would produce for that input. Demonstrates value in the UI. (display, agent)

owner: string — optional. Team or person who maintains this skill. (display)
